boards.title: Claimed by 9am: 10 Study Spots Worth Showing Up Early For
boards.description: Ten distinct University of Chicago Library environments, spanning quiet reading rooms, collection-adjacent tables, and reservable group spaces.

cards.title: Mansueto Grand Reading Room
cards.subtitle: Joe and Rika Mansueto Library
cards.notes: Bring work that benefits from a quiet shared room; the 8,000-square-foot space sits beneath the south side of Mansueto’s glass dome.
cards.short_summary: A large, quiet reading room under the library’s glass dome.
cards.evidence_claim: The Library describes the 180-seat Grand Reading Room as an 8,000-square-foot space designed for quiet study; food is not allowed.
cards.source_title: Library Spaces — University of Chicago Library
cards.access_notes: Listed as a quiet zone with public computers, copy/print/scan, and large tables; no food.

cards.title: Regenstein 2nd Floor Reading Room
cards.subtitle: Joseph Regenstein Library
cards.notes: Choose this floor when you want quiet with a choice of carrels, individual and large tables, standing desks, or softer seating.
cards.short_summary: Quiet study with varied furniture and dual-monitor stations.
cards.evidence_claim: The Library identifies this as a quiet study area with varied furniture, including carrels, standing desks, individual tables, and dual-monitor stations.
cards.source_title: Library Spaces — University of Chicago Library
cards.access_notes: Listed as a quiet zone; snacks are allowed, and lockers, public computers, printing, and dual monitors are available.

cards.title: Regenstein 3rd Floor Reading Room
cards.subtitle: Joseph Regenstein Library
cards.notes: Set up here for quiet work that needs scanning or a range of desk formats, then use the nearby collections as needed.
cards.short_summary: Quiet reading-room seating with an overhead book scanner.
cards.evidence_claim: The Library says the 3rd Floor Reading Room provides quiet study, varied furniture, and specialized equipment including an overhead book scanner.
cards.source_title: Library Spaces — University of Chicago Library
cards.access_notes: Listed as a quiet zone with snacks allowed, printing, public computers, carrels, standing desks, lockers, and an overhead book scanner.

cards.title: Classics Reading Room (Room 470)
cards.subtitle: Joseph Regenstein Library, 4th Floor
cards.notes: Use the large tables and dual-monitor stations for focused work, while yielding priority seating to people using the Classics reference collection.
cards.short_summary: A quiet, reference-collection reading room with dual monitors.
cards.evidence_claim: The Library calls Room 470 a quiet study space with public computers, dual-monitor stations, and large tables; Classics-reference users have priority.
cards.source_title: Library Spaces — University of Chicago Library
cards.access_notes: Quiet zone; snacks are allowed. Priority should be given to patrons using the Classics reference collection.

cards.title: Map Collection Reading Room
cards.subtitle: Joseph Regenstein Library, Room 370
cards.notes: Bring a project that benefits from a large table, and leave room for researchers consulting the Map Collection, who receive seating priority.
cards.short_summary: A quiet collection-adjacent room with large tables.
cards.evidence_claim: The Library states that Room 370 houses the Map Collection, provides quiet study space, and gives priority to patrons using that collection.
cards.source_title: Library Spaces — University of Chicago Library
cards.access_notes: Listed as a quiet zone with snacks allowed and large tables; Map Collection users have priority.

cards.title: Regenstein Group Studies
cards.subtitle: Joseph Regenstein Library, 2nd–5th Floor Reading Rooms
cards.notes: Reserve one for a group of two or more and plan around the three-hour daily booking limit; rooms include large tables and whiteboards.
cards.short_summary: Reservable group rooms distributed across four reading-room floors.
cards.evidence_claim: The Library lists 17 Regenstein group studies, reservable by groups of two or more for up to three hours daily whenever Regenstein is open.
cards.source_title: Reservable Library Study Spaces — University of Chicago Library
cards.access_notes: Reservable via Book a Room whenever Regenstein is open; groups of two or more may reserve up to three hours per day.

cards.title: Crerar 010 Reading Room
cards.subtitle: John Crerar Library
cards.notes: Use this quiet room for individual reading or desk work, especially if a large table and snack-permitted setting suit the session.
cards.short_summary: A quiet Crerar reading room with large tables.
cards.evidence_claim: The Library identifies Crerar 010 as a quiet study space for University of Chicago students, staff, and faculty, with large tables.
cards.source_title: John Crerar Library Spaces — University of Chicago Library
cards.access_notes: Quiet zone; snacks are allowed. The Library specifies eligibility for University of Chicago students, staff, and faculty.

cards.title: Crerar Group Studies
cards.subtitle: John Crerar Library, Lower Level
cards.notes: Book one of the two lower-level rooms for a collaborative session, using the large tables and whiteboards to organize shared work.
cards.short_summary: Two reservable lower-level rooms for collaborative work.
cards.evidence_claim: The Library states that two Crerar group study rooms can be booked by current University of Chicago students, staff, and faculty.
cards.source_title: John Crerar Library Spaces — University of Chicago Library
cards.access_notes: Reservable group-study rooms on the Lower Level; current University of Chicago students, staff, and faculty may book them.

cards.title: Center for Digital Scholarship
cards.subtitle: Joseph Regenstein Library, 1st Floor
cards.notes: Work on a digital project at a specialty-software workstation or gather collaborators around the large tables and whiteboards; food is not allowed.
cards.short_summary: A collaborative digital-research space with specialty software.
cards.evidence_claim: The Library describes the Center for Digital Scholarship as a first-floor collaborative space with six specialty-software workstations, large tables, and comfortable seating.
cards.source_title: Library Spaces — University of Chicago Library
cards.access_notes: Collaboration zone with public computers, standing desks, whiteboards, and day lockers; no food.

cards.title: Social Work Library Reading Room
cards.subtitle: Social Work Library
cards.notes: Schedule daytime reading here when you want natural light; the southern wall has floor-to-ceiling windows in a large open reading room.
cards.short_summary: A bright reading room with floor-to-ceiling southern windows.
cards.evidence_claim: The Library describes the Social Work Library reading room as a large open space with southern floor-to-ceiling windows that provide natural light during the day.
cards.source_title: Library Spaces — University of Chicago Library
cards.access_notes: Listed as an open study space with individual tables; no food is allowed.
